title: Orbital Momentum Transfer Lab
description: A DamagedHelmet floats at the center of a zero-gravity arena while multiple WaterBottles orbit it at varying radii. The user adjusts each bottle's tangential velocity, transfers angular momentum between bottles via elastic collisions, and uses undo/redo to explore conservation of total angular momentum across the system.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a zero-gravity orbital momentum transfer simulation. Load DamagedHelmet.glb and place it at the origin as a massive central body with a subtle glow (PointLight inside). Load WaterBottle.glb and instantiate 4 clones placed in circular orbits at radii 3, 4.5, 6, and 7.5 units in the XZ plane. Each bottle orbits the helmet under an inverse-square gravitational pull. Use OrbitControls for camera (start at position [0,8,14] looking at origin). Add ambient light (0.3) and a directional light from upper-right. Display a HUD panel (HTML overlay) showing: total system angular momentum L_total, each bottle's individual L_i, and kinetic energy. The user can click a bottle to select it (highlight with outline or emissive color), then use a slider to apply a tangential impulse (positive or negative), which changes that bottle's orbital velocity. Enforce conservation: when one bottle's momentum changes, prompt the user to pick a second bottle to receive the equal-and-opposite impulse transfer, simulating an elastic momentum exchange via a visible dashed-line tether that briefly appears. Track L_total and display a warning if conservation is violated beyond 1% tolerance. Implement full undo/redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) using a state stack that records each impulse pair. Add a 'Reset Orbits' button. The simulation loop uses semi-implicit Euler integration each frame. Bottles that fall below radius 1.5 collide with the helmet (bounce elastically, flash red). Bottles escaping beyond radius 12 are clamped back with a warning. Add a step counter showing completed interaction steps out of 12 target steps (select, impulse, pair, confirm counts as one step). Use a subtle star-field background (BufferGeometry points). All physics values (mass, G constant) should be displayed in a collapsible info panel.
